measures.title: Permanent Base Adjustment
measures.summary: Referred by the Pima County Board of Supervisors, it asks voters to permanently raise the state-set 1979-80 expenditure base for Pima County by $70,000,000, adjusted each year for population and inflation. The official summary says this would raise the County's spending limit in fiscal year 2027-2028 from $817,131,286 to $1,427,217,767, with the added authority usable for any local budget purpose.
measures.yesMeans: Pima County may permanently adjust its 1979-80 base expenditure limit upward by $70,000,000.
measures.noMeans: Pima County's 1979-80 base expenditure limit is not adjusted.

measures.title: Pima County Community College District Special Bond Election
measures.summary: Asks whether Pima County Community College District may issue and sell up to $250,000,000 in general obligation bonds for land, buildings, equipment and facilities, with listed potential uses including first-responder training, moving police headquarters to the Downtown Campus, and updating student services, teacher education, IT, arts and STEM programs. The bonds would mature in 1 to 20 years at interest up to 10% per year and would be repaid with a secondary property tax increase.
measures.yesMeans: The District may issue and sell $250,000,000 of general obligation bonds repaid with secondary property taxes.
measures.noMeans: The District may not issue and sell these bonds.

measures.title: Proposed Electric Transmission and Distribution Franchise
measures.summary: Asks City of Tucson voters to grant Tucson Electric Power Company a franchise to build, maintain and operate electric transmission and distribution facilities in the city's public rights-of-way. In return the City would receive a franchise fee and other consideration.
measures.yesMeans: A franchise for electric transmission and distribution services is granted to Tucson Electric Power Company.
measures.noMeans: The franchise for electric transmission and distribution services to Tucson Electric Power Company is denied.

measures.title: Gene Reid Park Zoo Sales Tax Reauthorization (Tucson Charter, Chapter IV, Section 5)
measures.summary: A charter amendment referred by the Mayor and Council that would reauthorize the City's one-tenth-cent (0.1%) sales and use tax for another twenty years, from January 1, 2028 to December 31, 2047. The revenue would stay dedicated to capital improvements, infrastructure repair and replacement, exhibit expansion, and related operations and maintenance at the Gene Reid Park Zoo.
measures.yesMeans: The 0.1% sales and use tax for the Gene Reid Park Zoo is reauthorized through December 31, 2047.
measures.noMeans: The 0.1% sales and use tax for the Gene Reid Park Zoo is not reauthorized beyond December 31, 2027.
